options.content:
One stream of SYN packets to one server; each sample is one packet, and its value is the packet's source IP address. The synthetic data runs 30 minutes with 1 series per metric. | column | what it is | values | |---|---|---| | time | Time of the sample | One sample every 1 ms (1,000 per second) | | vm | The server under attack; there is only one, instance1 | instance1 | | src_ip | Source IP address of the packet, as an integer | Usual values: Zipf distribution (skew 1.1) over 2,000 values
Minutes 5 to 11, ramping in and out over 30 s: 60% of samples are random values, uniform over the whole numbers 1,000,000 to 4,294,967,295; 25× as many samples per second
Minutes 20 to 24, ramping in and out over 60 s: 40% of samples are random values, uniform over the whole numbers 1,000,000 to 4,294,967,295; 10× as many samples per second
Note: whole numbers; the planner is told to expect at most 10,000 distinct values per evaluation |

Each query runs twice, once with the exact plan and once with the approximate plan. A rule reads query results and decides an action; exact and approx decide separately, and the dashboard compares their decisions. On the time charts below, shaded areas are the problem periods injected into the synthetic data.

**Queries**

| query | PromQL | computed |
|---|---|---|
| entropy_10s | `entropy_over_time(src_ip{vm="instance1"}[10s])` | every 5 s over the last 10 s |
| distinct_10s | `distinct_over_time(src_ip{vm="instance1"}[10s])` | every 5 s over the last 10 s |
| distinct_5s | `distinct_over_time(src_ip{vm="instance1"}[5s])` | every 5 s over the last 5 s |
| packets_5s | `count_over_time(src_ip{vm="instance1"}[5s])` | every 5 s over the last 5 s |
| distinct_1m | `distinct_over_time(src_ip{vm="instance1"}[1m])` | every 5 s over the last 60 s |

**Rules**

| rule | queries it uses | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| entropy_10s > 8.5 | entropy_10s | Fires at every evaluation where entropy_10s is above 8.5, with no waiting period (one of the PromSketch thresholds, taken one query at a time) |
| distinct_10s > 3,000 | distinct_10s | Fires at every evaluation where distinct_10s is above 3,000 addresses, with no waiting period (one of the PromSketch thresholds, taken one query at a time) |
| distinct_5s > 1,700 | distinct_5s | Fires at every evaluation where distinct_5s is above 1,700 addresses, with no waiting period (one of the PromSketch thresholds, taken one query at a time) |
| packets_5s > 100,000 | packets_5s | Fires at every evaluation where packets_5s is above 100,000 packets, with no waiting period (threshold ours) |
| distinct_1m > 18,000 | distinct_1m | Fires at every evaluation where distinct_1m is above 18,000 addresses, with no waiting period (threshold ours) |
| promsketch_for_15s | entropy_10s, distinct_10s, distinct_5s | Any of the PromSketch thresholds (entropy_10s > 8.5, distinct_10s > 3,000, distinct_5s > 1,700) holds for 15 s: firing at the 4th evaluation in a row, as Prometheus does with for: 15s at a 5 s interval (Red Hat) |
| datadog | distinct_10s | Distinct source IPs over 10 s above the mean plus 3 standard deviations of the previous 5 minutes (Datadog baseline deviation; window and width ours) |
| kentik | distinct_10s | Distinct source IPs over 10 s above 200% of the mean of the previous 5 minutes, at least 3 times in the last 6 evaluations (Kentik; X, Y and baseline window ours) |
| netflow_logic | entropy_10s | One-sided CUSUM on source IP entropy: mean and standard deviation from the first 50 evaluations, slack 0.5 and alarm at 5 standard deviations (NetFlow Logic patent; parameters ours) |
| fastnetmon | packets_5s | More than 20,000 packets per second averaged over 5 s; ban for 1,900 s, and until the attack ends (FastNetMon defaults with unban_only_if_attack_finished) |
| red_hat | distinct_1m | More than 300 SYN-only flows per second over 1 minute for 15 s, counting each source address as one flow; firing at the 4th evaluation in a row (Red Hat Network Observability; flows as distinct sources ours) |

panels.title: Every run and query: plan, query error, and what the application saw
panels.description: Each row is one query in one run, paired with one rule or alert that reads it; a query read by three rules has three rows. Sketch and parameters are the approximate plan the planner chose: the sketch type and its size (for KMV, k is how many hashes it keeps; for HLL, precision p means 2^p registers). Fidelity compares the rule's decisions on the exact and approx answers: an episode is a stretch of consecutive evaluations where the exact rule fires, an incident is an attack or change the data generator injected (synthetic data only). Hover a fidelity cell to read all of it.

properties.value: Defined per application. Threshold alert: evaluations where exact and approx agree on firing. Autoscaler: matched scaling actions over matched, false and missed ones. Rollout controller: rollouts decided the same. Top clients: mean clients shared by the exact and approx top lists, as a fraction of the list size. Rule: entity-evaluations where exact and approx agree on whether the rule is active.
